component: P16 six structural schemas and offline conformance tooling
constraints: Publish closed versioned JSON contracts consumable outside one language; schemas are trusted repository inputs, not arbitrary uploaded programs.
Check finite local fixtures with external reference retrieval denied and no coercion; structure must not substitute for byte validation, authentication or time policy.
No deployment target, throughput SLA or hard deadline is specified for this developer/CI tooling.
alternatives: JSON Schema 2020-12 with Python jsonschema and an explicitly non-retrieving Registry.
JavaScript/TypeScript Ajv compiled JSON Schema with coercion disabled and trusted schemas.
Rust jsonschema with explicit retrieval and regex configuration.
CUE closed definitions and constraint unification, with JSON Schema import/export interoperability reviewed separately.
rationale: KEEP JSON Schema as the published contract: it preserves a standard, independently consumable structural boundary rather than making one language model the exchange format.

KEEP the offline Python checker for direct comparison with the real Python APIs and explicit reference rejection. Ajv and Rust are credible alternate engines; no specified workload or measured advantage establishes a migration winner.

CUE offers a constraint-oriented model but replacing the published standard requires demonstrated semantic equivalence for the existing contracts. Installation, familiarity and rewrite cost are not selection criteria.

Correct the ADR reference pattern now: whitespace exclusion admitted raw controls, non-URI punctuation and malformed percent escapes. An explicit ASCII character profile and percent triplets fixes the demonstrated defect without relying on optional format checks.

Nineteen focused schema methods pass, including 22 portable reference cases. Node ECMAScript patterns in normal and Unicode modes agree on all 22 cases; this is pattern evidence, not complete validator parity.
limits: The ADR profile restricts characters; it is not a complete URI, DNS, source-credibility or dereference validator. Encoded controls remain URI data; no decoding or network request occurs.
Integral floats can satisfy JSON Schema; duplicate JSON keys, byte bounds, signatures, intervals, key bindings and cross-field uniqueness still require runtime checks.
Python regex semantics are not universally ECMAScript-equivalent. The Node probe covers only this fixed pattern and finite corpus.
No full Ajv, Rust or CUE implementation was executed or benchmarked. No migration winner is deferred.
This review does not complete the lane, attest a distribution or establish MLS/CNSA, availability or physical timing. Insufficient information for tactical deployment.
